newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Hongkong Bank Philippine unit eyes retail business.
newsitem.headline: Hongkong Bank Philippine unit eyes retail business.

text.p: The Philippine unit of HSBC Holdings plc plans to target affluent Filipinos' growing needs by offering personal finance and retail banking services, bank officials said on Tuesday.

"I think this is the right time to go into personal and consumer financing. The demand for housing and consumer loans will grow hand in hand with the economy," Brian Fredrick, chief executive of Hongkong Bank Philippines, told reporters at a news conference.
"We are very positive about the Philippines. We are not only going to expand our branch network but also expand the breadth of our business and the scope of our business," he added.
The bank will target professionals and middle-tiered managers whose disposable income as well as financing demand are bound to grow as the economy expands.
Last year, the bank launched its credit card service as its initial foray into the consumer banking business.
"We will see more products in the runway which will take off starting this year," he said, but declined to elaborate.
Hongkong Bank Philippines is a unit of HSBC Holdings Plc.
Personal and retail banking services have long been the stronghold of local commercial banks whose branch networks extend deep into the countryside.
Consumer loans have been on the rise in the past few years as interest rates improved because of the strengthening economy.
Loans extended by the commercial banks have grown four-fold since 1991.
Fredrick said the advancement of information technology had made it possible for banks to widen their customer base through telephones and personal computers.
"The competition now is on technology and delivery system," he added.
Hongkong Bank is limited to only eight branches throughout the country. At present, it has four branches in key business districts.
Hongkong Bank, which has already been operating in the country for 122 years, has created a niche in securities custodianship, foreign exchange and securities trading and corporate banking.
Fredrick said he expected the bank's retail banking division to contribute 40 percent of its bottom line in five years' time.
Deputy chief executive officer Paul Lawrence said the bank would continue to pursue project financing and corporate banking.
The bank is presently looking at several infrastructure projects, notably toll road projects, for possible financing.
Hong Kong Bank Philippines posted a 37 percent increase in its net income last year to 485.76 million pesos ($18.47 million), while revenues grew by 30 percent.
Interest income rose by more than 69 percent and commissions by 23 percent.
